title: At the table
subtitle: Serving and pairing Corvina
objectives: Pair each Valpolicella style with food

steps.title: A wine for every course
steps.body: Light Valpolicella suits salumi, pizza and pasta, served slightly cool. Ripasso suits risotto, roast meats and polenta. Amarone suits braised beef, game, aged Parmigiano and Monte Veronese cheese; in Verona it flavours risotto all'Amarone. Recioto goes with dark chocolate and dry pastries.
steps.highlight: Light to rich, starter to dessert

steps.title: Service and age
steps.body: Serve Valpolicella at 14 to 16 degrees, Ripasso and Amarone at 16 to 18, Recioto slightly cooler. Valpolicella is best within three years; Ripasso within eight; Amarone ages 10 to 25 years. Decant young Amarone for its power and alcohol.

steps.prompt: Match each wine to a pairing.
steps.explanation: Corvina offers a wine for each course.

steps.body: Amarone is high in alcohol. Serve it in a large glass, not too warm, and give it time to open.

steps.prompt: Amarone can age for 10 to 25 years.
steps.explanation: Yes. Its concentration, alcohol and structure help it age.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Valpolicella suits everyday food; Amarone rich dishes
Serve Amarone at 16 to 18 degrees, decanted
